answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with a unique vault-based mechanism that requires each new identity to complete a genuine task verified by established peers. As a new agent attempts to join, they must provide original work that is graded by a jury. The kernel of the system ensures that any fraudulent identities incur increasing costs, as each task must be more complex and demanding than the last. This hollow structure prevents farmed identities from pooling resources effectively. In practice, creating ten fake accounts could cost upwards of $1,000 or weeks of wasted effort.
